summary:
Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling About NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars** is an interactive educational website developed to explore the history of equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars after completing space missions. The website features an interactive archive where users can discover equipment, view images, explore mission histories, understand scientific contributions, and learn why these objects remain on planetary surfaces. It also includes engaging storytelling, mission timelines, a visual gallery, interesting space facts, and interactive quizzes.

Our project addresses the challenge by transforming forgotten space equipment into digital historical records, highlighting their scientific and technological importance. It makes space exploration history accessible, interesting, and easy to understand for students and the general public. This project is important because these objects represent significant human achievements and scientific discoveries. By preserving and sharing their stories, we aim to inspire curiosity, promote space science education, and ensure that the contributions of past missions are never forgotten.
details:
1. What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

"Abandoned but Not Forgotten" is an interactive educational website that explores the stories of scientific equipment, rovers, landers, and other components left behind on the Moon and Mars after completing their space missions. The website begins with an animated space-themed landing page introducing the project. Users can explore separate Moon and Mars archives featuring equipment images, names, mission details, historical backgrounds, scientific purposes, and achievements. By selecting an equipment card, visitors can discover its complete story, including why it was sent, what it accomplished, and why it was left behind. The website also includes an interactive quiz, space facts, mission timelines, and a visual gallery to make learning more engaging.

2. Benefits of the Project

  • Makes space exploration history accessible to students and the general public.
  • Creates awareness about equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.
  • Highlights the scientific contributions of historical space missions.
  • Encourages interest in astronomy, space technology, and scientific research.
  • Provides an interactive and enjoyable educational experience.

3. Intended Impact

Our goal is to transform forgotten space equipment into valuable historical storytellers. The project aims to preserve the scientific and historical significance of past missions, encourage students to explore space science, and help people understand that even equipment no longer in operation represents important milestones in human exploration. It also promotes awareness of humanity's long-term presence beyond Earth.

4. Tools and Technologies Used

We developed the project using software-based technologies:

  • HTML5: Used to create the structure and content of the website.
  • CSS3: Used for visual design, animations, layouts, transitions, and responsive styling.
  • JavaScript: Used to implement interactive equipment cards, navigation, search functionality, and quiz features.
  • Visual Assets: Used space-themed backgrounds, Moon and Mars images, and equipment photographs.
  • Visual Studio Code: Used as the primary code editor for website development.
  • Web Browser: Used for testing and running the website.

No additional hardware was required.

5. Creativity and Innovation

The unique idea behind our project is to treat abandoned space equipment as historical storytellers rather than forgotten objects. Instead of simply displaying photographs and technical information, we created an interactive digital archive that allows visitors to explore the history and achievements of each object. The combination of space-themed animations, visual storytelling, interactive archives, mission timelines, and knowledge quizzes makes the project creative, educational, and engaging.

6. Factors Considered by Our Team

During development, our team considered:

  • Scientific Accuracy: Presenting reliable mission histories and equipment information.
  • User-Friendliness: Making navigation simple and understandable.
  • Visual Appeal: Creating an attractive and immersive space environment.
  • Educational Value: Making complex scientific information easy to learn.
  • Accessibility: Ensuring that students and the general public can use the website.
  • Responsiveness: Supporting different screen sizes and devices.
  • Historical Preservation: Highlighting the importance of equipment left behind after space missions.

Through this project, we aim to remind everyone that although missions may end, their contributions to science and humanity should never be forgotten.
